questions.q: What is the main point of the passage?
options: Skilled mechanics should build each car by hand from start to finish
Saved time and motion let unskilled men produce well under skilled planning
Wages should be set by the employer's generosity rather than output
Each part should be made by one worker doing every operation
questions.explain: The author builds production on saved motion, putting skill into planning and tools so unskilled men can work.

questions.q: Saving ten steps a day for twelve thousand employees saves how much wasted motion?
questions.explain: He says saving ten steps for each of twelve thousand employees saves fifty miles of wasted motion.

questions.q: Which was the first motor Ford made entirely themselves?
questions.explain: The Model T was the first motor that they made themselves.

questions.q: What was the first step forward in assembly?
options: Hiring more skilled machinists to run each department
Taking the work to the men instead of the men to the work
Building taller factories to save ground space
Putting one department in charge of making every small part
questions.explain: The first step forward came when they began taking the work to the men instead of the men to the work.

questions.q: According to the author, what actually pays workers' wages?
questions.explain: He says it is not the employer who pays wages; the product pays them, and management arranges production for it.
